chunks: And it is narrated from Dāwūd ibn al-Ḥuṣayn, from ʿUmar ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who said to another: 'Propose so-and-so to me, and whatever you do of anything you negotiate regarding dowry, or guarantee of anything, or stipulate, then that is acceptable to me and binding upon me.' But he did not bring witnesses to that. So he went and proposed on his behalf, and offered the dowry for him and other than that from what they demanded of him and asked of him. Then when he returned, he denied all of that.

He said: 'Half of the dowry is imposed for her against him, on his behalf, and that is because he is the one who caused her right to be lost. So when he did not have her witness against him regarding that which he said to him, it became lawful for her to marry, and she is not lawful for the first one, in what is between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, unless he divorces her, because Allah, the Exalted, says:'
“Then retention in a fair manner or release with kindness.”

So if he does not do that, then he is sinful in what is between him and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. And the outward ruling is the ruling of Islam, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has made it lawful for her to marry.

key_terms.الْحُكْمُ الظَّاهِرُ: the outward legal ruling applied in Islamic law
key_terms.حَقَّهَا: her legal right in the marriage matter
key_terms.شَرَطْتَ: you stipulated conditions in the agreement
key_terms.صَدَاقٍ: dowry agreed for the marriage contract
key_terms.نِصْفَ الصَّدَاقِ: half of the dowry owed in this case
key_terms.يُغَرَّمُ: he is made financially liable to pay

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone authorizes a marriage proposal through an agent and then denies the agreement?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about agency in marriage arrangements when a man authorizes another to negotiate on his behalf but fails to secure proof of that authorization. If he later denies the arrangement, financial liability remains, the woman may marry someone else according to the outward Islamic ruling, and the man is accountable before Allah if he withholds divorce unjustly.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3384 - It is narrated from Dawood ibn Al-Husayn, from Umar ibn Hanzalah, from Abu Abdullah (as):

I asked him about a man who said to another, "Propose marriage to so-and-so on my behalf, and whatever you negotiate regarding the dowry, guarantee, or conditions will be binding on me and accepted."
However, he did not bring witnesses for this agreement. The second man went ahead, proposed marriage, and committed to the dowry and other demands they requested. When he returned, the first man denied all of it.

Imam (as) said: "He must pay half of the dowry on his behalf, as it was he who neglected her right by failing to have witnesses for the agreement he made. Thus, it becomes permissible for her to marry someone else, and the first man is not allowed to take her back unless he formally divorces her. This is because Allah (swt) the Exalted says:
'Retention in kindness or release in fairness'

(Surah Al-Baqarah 2:229). If he does not do so, then he is sinful before Allah (swt) the Almighty. However, the apparent ruling under Islamic law allows her to marry someone else, as Allah (swt) has made it permissible for her."
